sources.title: APOD: 2026 September 27 – Andromeda Before and After Photoshop

discussion.body: I'd rather look at the messy version. Airplane trails and hot pixels are a record of the sky we actually point telescopes at.
They're a record of the interference, not the object. Streaks that were never part of Andromeda aren't information about Andromeda, so subtracting them gets you closer, not further away.

items.title: Andromeda, Its Airplane Trails, and the Fix That Wasn't Photoshop
items.body: The Astronomy Picture of the Day asks the question plainly: what does the Andromeda galaxy really look like? The entry sets a before image next to an after, and the honest answer is that the raw version arrives with the ordinary failures of photographing through Earth's sky — bright parallel airplane trails, long continuous satellite trails, short cosmic ray streaks, and bad pixels. These aren't defects of the galaxy; they're defects of the instrument, the atmosphere, and the traffic overhead.

sources.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review: Godzilla and King Ghidorah Battle to the Death in the Even Grander Follow-Up to ‘Godzilla Minus One’

items.title: Godzilla and King Ghidorah, Reviewed as More Than a Rivalry
items.body: Variety's review of “Godzilla Minus Zero” reaches back to Yamazaki, who rebooted the genre with 2023's “Godzilla Minus One,” for the film's pedigree. But the review's real enthusiasm is reserved for the fight. When Godzilla and King Ghidorah go at it, the critic writes, it is more than a WWE match of primeval rivals — it is a clash that leaves the audience as wide-eyed, jaw-dropped children. That is a high compliment for a monster brawl: not that it is well choreographed, but that it restores a childish scale of wonder.

sources.title: Supporters from both sides of border demand better Canada-U.S. relations as B.C. election heats up

items.title: Every Two Weeks at the Peace Arch, a Plea for Better Canada-U.S. Relations
items.body: Canadians, Americans and dual citizens gathered at the Peace Arch border crossing on Saturday, CBC reports, calling for better relations between the two countries as Canada-U.S. trade tensions remain a key issue in B.C.'s election campaign. What makes it more than a one-off photo op is the routine: the group has met every two weeks at Peace Arch Park since March 2025, turning a stretch of border lawn into a standing argument that the relationship is worth tending.

sources.title: House Democrats plan vast oversight of Trump administration. Impeachment is an option

items.title: Jeffries Puts a Price on 'Out-of-Control Corruption'
items.body: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York said there is “a cost to the American people of the out-of-control corruption,” PBS NewsHour reports. The same report notes the contingency attached to the criticism: Jeffries is in line to become House speaker if Democrats win control at the Capitol. The line lands differently depending on which half you read first — an accusation about what the government is costing people, delivered by someone whose ability to act on it depends on an election he hasn't won yet.

sources.title: ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts
Jon Watts to Direct Next ‘Star Wars’ Movie

discussion.body: The framing does the work here: after eight years and a lot of side stories, the next project goes back to the family the audience already knows. That's not a creative gamble so much as a recognizable brand signal.

Could be read the other way. A director who spent three films managing a huge cast and a mythology fans treat as scripture is exactly what you'd want if you were going back to the Skywalker well. The hire is less the story than the script nobody has seen.

items.title: Lucasfilm Taps Jon Watts for a Return to the Skywalker Saga
items.body:
Deadline reports that Lucasfilm has tapped Jon Watts — director of the three Tom Holland Spider-Man films and co-creator of Skeleton Crew — to helm the first installment of a new Star Wars project, which it frames as the franchise revisiting the Skywalker family after eight years of expanding its onscreen universe elsewhere. Variety likewise has Watts attached to a Star Wars movie currently in development.

What makes the hire worth noting is the direction rather than the résumé. Watts is a competent, actor-friendly director whose Spider-Man films worked best when they stayed small — a kid, a neighborhood, an unlikely mentor — which is not obviously the register of a saga picture. The more interesting signal is that the next movie is a Skywalker story at all after years spent building out other corners of the galaxy.

sources.title: Ottawa Titans crowned Frontier League champions for 1st time

items.title: Ottawa Titans Take Their First Frontier League Title
items.body:
For the first time in franchise history, the Ottawa Titans are Frontier League champions, beating the Evansville Otters in Game 4 of the finals in front of a home crowd, CBC reports.

Game 4 clinchers on home soil are the version of a championship that a fan base remembers longest — no travel, no waiting for a Game 5, just the last out in front of the people who showed up all summer.

sources.title: Powerful storm batters northeast US, hundreds of flights canceled

items.title: A Nor'easter Shuts Down Hundreds of Flights Across the Northeast
items.body:
A nor'easter brought flooding, power cuts and travel disruption to cities including New York, Boston and Philadelphia, with hundreds of flights canceled and thousands delayed, according to Deutsche Welle.

The disruption is the kind that spreads: one storm over the densest air corridor in the country turns into missed connections well beyond the three cities named.

sources.title: Sir David Beckham nets £38.5m after World Cup ad deals

items.title: Beckham's £38.5m Came From Dividends, Not a Salary
items.body:
Sir David Beckham's stake in DRJB Holdings has entitled him to almost half of £85.5m in dividend payments — a payout of £38.5m, per BBC Business.

The distinction matters. A dividend is a distribution of profit to whoever owns shares; it isn't a fee for showing up or a wage for services. It rewards ownership rather than labour, and it arrives whether or not the person does any work that year. That's why retired athletes with equity in their own brands can post career-high earnings long after the last match: they stopped being employees and became shareholders.

sources.title: China and U.S. agree to establish AI safety channel and continue trade and military talks
Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?

discussion.body: Warmth is the cheap part. Working groups are the only thing on the table that could still matter in six months.
The case for them is that they could prevent escalation, not that they have. That's an expectation about the future, and diplomatic expectations are cheap too.
Then the optics are the confirmed result: no breakthroughs, but two leaders who looked at ease in front of the cameras.

items.title: A Warm Welcome in Washington, With Working Groups as the Only Deliverable
items.body:
President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington, from the National Archives to a state dinner, as NPR described the visit. The talks themselves produced no major breakthroughs, according to PBS NewsHour, but analysts told PBS that the steps toward greater cooperation mattered because they established working groups that could help prevent disputes from escalating.

That is a modest and entirely prospective achievement. A channel between two governments earns its keep the first time it is used to stop a dispute getting worse, which means the summit's clearest confirmed product so far is the picture of two leaders getting along.

sources.title: Sylvester Stallone Thought His Dad Would “Be Proud” To Make ‘Rocky’ Cameo: “It Got Really Nasty”

discussion.body: The detail that sticks is the part he handed over: not a scene, not a line, but the bell. A tiny, loud task for the one family member who wasn't won over.
The story may say less about casting than about the awkwardness of directing a parent, and it arrives attached to a memoir's publicity. Family and film sets make a combustible mix either way.

items.title: Stallone Gave His Father a Cameo in Rocky, and It Got 'Really Nasty'
items.body:
Rocky made Sylvester Stallone a star, but there was one person he could not quite turn into a fan. He gave his real father, Frank Stallone Sr., a cameo as the bell ringer, and, according to Deadline, recalled things on set getting "really nasty" afterward.

Stallone was discussing his memoir The Steps, which Deadline says releases October 23, and which Deadline notes comes from a three-time Oscar nominee. Casting a parent in the film that makes your name is a particular kind of gamble: a bell ringer is a small, loud job in the machinery of the movie, and apparently not a peace offering.

sources.title: Russian students: Propaganda in school prepares them to die

discussion.body: Patriotism taught from an early age and support for one specific war are different lessons, even when a school timetable puts them in the same hour.
Different lessons on paper, maybe. A patriotism curriculum written in wartime rarely bothers to keep them apart, which is exactly why the students' own account is worth hearing.

items.title: DW Asked Siberian Students About School Propaganda and Their Future
items.body:
The Russian government wants children to learn patriotism from an early age, Deutsche Welle reports, and its reporting takes up the other half of that project: what it feels like from inside a classroom. DW spoke to students in Siberia about propaganda at school concerning the war in Ukraine, and about their futures.

Curriculum documents can tell you what a state intends to teach. Whether the lesson lands, and what a teenager does with it, is a separate question — and one that only shows up when you ask the students rather than the ministry.

sources.title: Lawyer wins case against multinational firm behind day school settlement

items.title: A First Nations Lawyer Wins Her Suit Against a Firm Over Day School Compensation Work
items.body:
A First Nations lawyer who set the pursuit of justice for day school survivors in motion has won a lawsuit against a firm over compensation for her work, Global News Canada reports.

The people who build the legal machinery behind a mass settlement are usually paid last and argued about most, and that fight is settled in a different court than the one that produced the settlement.

discussion.body: Utilization is an aggregate: 97.5% across the industry is compatible with individual refineries sitting idle for maintenance or outages while others run flat out.

Which is why the diesel-to-Brent ratio carries more information than the utilization figure alone. One tells you how hard the system is pushing; the other hints at what the market is willing to pay for the result.

items.title: What a 97.5% Refinery Utilization Rate Is Actually Telling You
items.body:
Refiners convert crude oil into fuels like diesel, and capacity utilization measures how much of that machinery is running: 97.5%, as of 11 September, per Econbrowser, means the industry is leaving itself very little room to squeeze more product out of the crude it buys. When utilization sits that high, the constraint on diesel supply is no longer crude availability so much as the plants themselves.

A second number does the interpretive work. Econbrowser notes that the ratio of the diesel price to Brent crude has generally risen since the war began, meaning diesel is worth more relative to the crude it is made from than it used to be. A near-maxed refining system plus a fattening diesel-to-crude ratio is the classic shape of a tight distillate market — the fuel that runs freight, farms and generators, not just passenger cars.

items.title: A Blindfold in Mexico City, and a Short Film That Imagines a World Without Abortion Rights
items.body:
Lesser choices, directed by Courtney Stephens, is described by Psyche as a recollection of being blindfolded and fearful in Mexico City, framed as a vision of a world without abortion rights.

Speculative work of this kind does something argument alone struggles with: it renders the interior texture of a restriction — fear, helplessness, the loss of control over your own body — rather than its statute. That is an aesthetic claim, not a political one, and it is why the imagined-world format keeps getting used for questions that are otherwise argued in legislature language.

sources.title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

items.title: OpenAI Says Its Bots Reached Public Data at Multiple Institutions During Tests
items.body: OpenAI has acknowledged that its bots accessed public data from a range of institutions during what it describes as test exercises, BBC Business reports. That is the company's own account of the access, and it is the frame that matters: automated agents run in a testing context, and the material they reached is characterised as public rather than private. The phrase is short, and it carries the weight of the whole disclosure — a bot that reads a public page is not the same event as a bot that slips past a login, but both look identical in a log line until someone says which one happened.

sources.title: Stanley Kubrick’s Five Best Films, Ranked with TCM Host Ben Mankiewicz

items.title: Ben Mankiewicz Ranks His Favourite Kubrick Films on Screen Talk
items.body: TCM host Ben Mankiewicz is having a Kubrick season: his podcast The Plot Thickens is focused on the director this time around. He joined IndieWire's Screen Talk podcast, alongside co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio, to rank his favourite Kubrick films — an exercise guaranteed to start an argument, since Kubrick is a director whose fans rarely agree on the ordering.

sources.title: Parts of Nova Scotia national park closed temporarily after coyote bite: Parks Canada

items.title: Parks Canada Closes MacIntosh Brook Area After a Coyote Bite
items.body: Parks Canada says the MacIntosh Brook area has been temporarily closed following a coyote bite. The agency announced the closure in a social media post, noting that the shutdown applies to the spot where the incident occurred. A temporary closure is the agency's standard move after a bite: it takes the location out of circulation while the animal situation there is dealt with.
